headline: Earnings surge on margin rebound, debt shrinks sharply
summary_short: Phillips 66 posted Q2 2026 net income of $3,847M ($9.55 diluted EPS), up from $207M ($0.51/share) in Q1 as Refining swung to $3,062M of pre-tax income from $208M on wider realized margins; total debt fell $6.6B to $20.6B.
summary_long: Refining led the rebound: pre-tax income rose to $3.06B from $208M as realized margins jumped to $24.08/bbl from $10.11/bbl on wider crack spreads and favorable mark-to-market impacts, while crude throughput rose modestly to 186,860 mbbl. Midstream income rose to $785M (higher margins, no repeat of Q1's Winter Storm Fern impact); Chemicals to $404M (higher margins); Marketing and Specialties to $583M (favorable mark-to-market, higher marketing margins); Renewable Fuels to $544M (higher regulatory credits and mark-to-market gains). Net income reached $3.85B ($9.55 diluted EPS) versus $207M in Q1. Total debt fell $6.6B to $20.6B; net debt fell to $16.5B. Cash slipped to $4.1B from $5.15B. Buybacks were $379M; capex $726M. No forward guidance was issued in the release.

drivers.explanation: not explained in the release -- the exhibit gives no consolidated revenue line or commentary; it discloses only segment earnings, EBITDA, and cash-flow tables.
Diluted weighted-average shares were flat q/q (402.6M vs 403.3M), so the EPS move mirrors the ~18x increase in net income almost one-for-one.
Tracks diluted EPS growth; basic ($9.59) sits slightly above diluted ($9.55) because basic shares outstanding are fewer than the diluted count.

Broad-based segment recovery led by Refining (+$2,854M pre-tax on higher realized margins), plus Midstream, Chemicals, Marketing and Specialties, and Renewable Fuels all higher versus Q1's depressed base.
Cost of revenue grew 49.5% q/q, slower than revenue's 56.8%, expanding gross profit to $6.76B from $2.77B -- consistent with the release's disclosed margin recovery in Refining and Marketing.
Moves with the same segment-level margin recovery cited for net income; the release's own Adjusted EBITDA figure ($5,891M) rose on identical drivers.

Not fully reconciled in this exhibit beyond the disclosed summary figures: $7,259M of operating cash flow funded $726M of capex and $887M of shareholder returns (buybacks + dividends), against a much larger debt paydown.
Company states it decreased total debt by $6.6 billion to $20.6 billion during the quarter; the current-portion tag fell in step with that broader paydown.
Equity attributable to Phillips 66 rose 10.4% q/q, consistent with retaining most of the $3,847M of net income after $887M of shareholder returns.

CEO Mark Lashier cited the strength of operations and the value of the integrated portfolio, and reaffirmed the capital allocation framework of disciplined investment, dividends, buybacks and debt reduction.
